blocks.text: The Telugu short essay (**vyasam**, 200–250 words) tests clear, correct expression on a given topic. Like any essay it needs a tight **introduction (prastavana) – body (vishaya vivarana) – conclusion (mukthayimpu)**, in grammatically correct, idiomatic Telugu.

rows: Frame the topic + state the central idea.
2-3 short paragraphs, one idea each, with an example.
Correct grammar, apt vocabulary, natural idiom.

items: Outline 2-3 points before writing; keep paragraphs short.
Use **correct sandhi, vibhakti and grammar**; avoid spelling errors.
Enrich with an apt **proverb (sametha) or quotation** where natural.
Stay within the word limit and conclude crisply.

mainsAngles: Practise 200-250-word Telugu essays across descriptive, analytical and reflective topics.
Focus on grammatical correctness (sandhi, vibhakti) and idiomatic expression.

glossary.definition: The Telugu term for an essay.
The introduction of a Telugu essay/composition.
A Telugu proverb, useful for enriching essays.

sections.heading: Elaborating poetic / verse thought (padya bhava vistarana)

blocks.text: **Bhava vistarana** asks you to **expand and explain the idea of a verse or poetic line** (padyam) in prose — bringing out its **meaning, moral and relevance** in clear Telugu, without merely translating it.

rows: Read the padyam; identify its central thought/moral.
Express the core meaning in your own prose.
Explain with reasoning and an example/illustration.

items: Explain the **bhava (idea)**, don't just translate the words.
Use an **example or analogy** to illustrate the moral.
Draw on the rich **Telugu didactic verse** tradition (Vemana, Sumati satakam).
Keep the language clear and the moral relevant to life.

mainsAngles: Practise expanding satakam/padyam verses into clear prose explanations.
Bring out the moral and its life-relevance, not a literal translation.

glossary.definition: The elaboration/expansion of the idea of a verse into prose.
A Telugu genre of 100 didactic verses (e.g. Vemana, Sumati).

blocks.text: **Samgraha lekhanam** is a Telugu precis — a concise summary of about **one-third** the original length, capturing the **central idea and main points** in your own words, omitting examples and repetition.

rows: Main ideas only; omit examples, repetition, digressions.
Paraphrase in your own Telugu; don't copy sentences.
The precis must read smoothly on its own.

items: Read twice, underline key points, find the theme.
Draft, then **cut to ~1/3** and count words.
Use **your own words**; keep grammar correct.
Ensure the summary is self-contained and coherent.

mainsAngles: Practise reducing Telugu passages to one-third with only the main ideas.
Master coherent paraphrasing and word-counting under time limits.

glossary.definition: Telugu precis/summary writing (about one-third of the original).
The title/heading given to a precis or composition.

blocks.text: **Avagahana** (reading comprehension) tests understanding of a Telugu passage — its **main idea, details, inference and vocabulary** — with answers drawn **only from the passage**, in clear, correct Telugu.

rows: Locate the exact statement in the text.
What is implied — reason from the passage.
Meaning of a word as used in context.
Brief, in your own words, from the passage.

items: Skim for gist, then scan for specific answers.
Answer **only from the passage** — no outside knowledge.
Keep answers **brief, relevant and grammatically correct**.
For inference, stay within what the text supports.

mainsAngles: Practise skim-and-scan on Telugu passages and answer strictly from the text.
Handle main-idea, detail and inference questions concisely.

glossary.definition: A conclusion drawn from what a passage implies rather than states.

blocks.text: A Telugu **formal speech (upanyasam)** — including a press-conference address — needs a courteous **salutation, engaging opening, structured body and rousing close**, in persuasive, audience-aware Telugu.

rows: Respectful address to the chief guest, dignitaries & audience.
2-3 clear points with examples; logical flow.
Memorable ending — call to action / vision; thanks.
State facts clearly; anticipate and answer likely questions.

items: Open with a **greeting and hook**; name the occasion.
Use **direct address** and rhetorical devices.
Keep points few and clear; **end memorably** with thanks.
For a press conference, be **factual, clear and composed**.

mainsAngles: Practise Telugu speeches with salutation, hook, structured body and rousing close.

glossary.definition: A formal speech or address in Telugu.
The courteous opening address to dignitaries and audience.

blocks.text: This task is writing **statements/releases for publicity media** in Telugu — official announcements, awareness messages or press notes — in a **clear, factual, public-friendly** style suited to newspapers, radio or social media.

rows: Clear, informative title of the message.
State what the public should know or do.

items: Put the **most important information first**.
Use **simple, clear Telugu** accessible to the general public.
Keep it **factual and concise**; include the source.
For awareness messages, make the **call to action clear**.

mainsAngles: Practise clear, public-friendly Telugu media statements and awareness notes.
Use the inverted-pyramid structure with a clear message and attribution.

glossary.definition: An official message written for newspapers, radio or social media.
A structure placing the most important information first.

blocks.text: Telugu **letter writing (lekha)** covers both **formal (official) and informal (personal)** letters, each with its own format and tone — formal letters being polite, precise and purposeful; personal ones warm and natural.

rows: Sender's address and date at the top.

items: Match **format and tone** to formal vs personal.
State the **purpose early**; keep formal letters concise & polite.
Personal letters can be warm and natural.
Keep grammar and spelling correct.

mainsAngles: Practise both formal (official) and personal Telugu letters with correct format.
Match tone to purpose; keep formal letters concise and courteous.

glossary.definition: Official correspondence (precise, polite) versus personal letters (warm, natural).
